questions.question: What property must a material have for liquid particles to be able to move through it by diffusion?
options: It must be impermeable
It must be permeable
It must be magnetic
It must be completely solid and dense

questions.question: When conducting an experiment to observe a liquid diffusing into a jelly cube, what is typically seen over time?
options: The liquid changes color only on the very outer surface and never penetrates deeper
The liquid moves from the outside into the center of the jelly cube, changing its color
The jelly cube dissolves instantly and disappears
The liquid remains completely separate and forms a solid layer around the cube

questions.question: How does increasing the temperature affect the rate at which a liquid diffuses into a jelly cube?
options: It slows down the rate of diffusion
It speeds up the rate of diffusion
It has no effect whatsoever on the rate of diffusion
It stops diffusion completely because particles freeze

questions.question: If you compare diffusion in a small jelly cube and a large jelly cube, which one will have its center reached by the diffusing liquid first?
options: The small jelly cube, because the liquid has a shorter distance to travel to reach the center
The large jelly cube, because it has a larger surface area to attract the liquid
Both cubes will have their centers reached at the exact same time
Neither cube, because diffusion only occurs on the surface of the jelly

questions.question: Using particle theory, why does a higher temperature increase the rate of diffusion of a liquid into a jelly cube?
options: Particles have less energy and move more slowly
Particles gain energy and move faster, colliding and spreading quicker
The jelly particles expand and block the pathways
The liquid particles become larger and heavier

questions.question: Why can only certain substance particles pass through a selectively-permeable membrane?
options: Only particles that are small enough can fit through the tiny holes in the membrane
Only particles that are magnetic can pass through the membrane
Only particles with a negative charge are allowed to pass
Only water particles are physically capable of movement

questions.question: When particles of a substance diffuse through a selectively-permeable membrane, in which direction do they move?
options: Only from the outside to the inside
Only from the inside to the outside
In both directions across the membrane
They do not move through the membrane at all

questions.question: If there is a high concentration of glucose particles outside a selectively-permeable membrane and a low concentration inside, what is the predicted net movement of glucose?
options: Net movement will be out of the membrane
Net movement will be into the membrane
There will be no movement of particles at all
Particles will move out of the membrane until it is empty

questions.question: In an experiment using Visking tubing to represent a selectively-permeable membrane, what would you observe if starch is inside the tubing and water is outside?
options: Starch quickly diffuses out because starch particles are very small
Starch does not diffuse out because starch particles are too large to pass through the tubing pores
Water cannot enter the tubing at all
The tubing completely dissolves in the water

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding cell cytoplasm and the substances within it?
options: They are continuous fluids with no individual particles
They are made up of tiny particles that are constantly in motion
They consist only of empty space with no particles
They are made up of a single, giant, unbreakable particle

questions.question: How do small substance particles, like oxygen, move into and out of a cell?
options: By being actively pushed by microscopic cellular pumps
By diffusing through small holes in the cell membrane
By dissolving the cell membrane entirely to pass through
By passing through the cell wall only, ignoring the membrane

questions.question: Why are some substances, such as large proteins, unable to diffuse into a cell?
options: They are too large to fit through the holes in the cell membrane
They are rejected by the cell's electrical charge
They can only move through the cell membrane when it is damaged
They travel too fast to be caught by the cell membrane

questions.question: What makes a cell membrane 'selectively-permeable'?
options: It allows all substances to pass through freely without restriction
It only allows certain substances to diffuse through it while blocking others
It is completely impermeable to all substances under any conditions
It only allows substances to leave the cell but never enter

questions.question: What is the net movement of particles through a cell membrane?
options: Up a concentration gradient, from low to high concentration
Down a concentration gradient, from high to low concentration
Randomly, always resulting in more particles on one side
Only in the direction of gravity

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the movement and interaction of particles in a fluid?
options: They move in straight, organized lines without ever touching
They move in random directions and collide with each other all the time
They remain stationary until a force is applied to them
They only move when heated above boiling point

questions.question: In scientific terms, what is meant by the 'concentration' of a substance in a liquid or gas?
options: The total mass of the container holding the liquid or gas
The number of particles of that substance in a given volume
The speed at which the particles are moving
The temperature of the liquid or gas

questions.question: What is the definition of diffusion?
options: The active transport of particles requiring energy from the cell
The passive movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration
The movement of water molecules from a low solute concentration to a high solute concentration only
The chemical reaction that occurs when two different liquids are mixed together
